title: SDG 5 性別平等
footer: Teacher Dom · SDG #5 Gender Equality 性別平等

slides.eyebrow_en: A Bilingual Lesson for Junior High Students

strip.zh: 項全球目標，這是第 5 項

strip.en: Taiwan elects its first woman president
strip.zh: 年，台灣選出第一位女總統

strip.en: jobs that are only for boys or only for girls
strip.zh: 種工作只屬於男生或只屬於女生

lines.en: I grew up in Compton, California.
lines.zh: 我在美國加州的 Compton 長大。

lines.en: This is my third year of teaching in Changhua.
lines.zh: 這是我在彰化教書的第三年。

lines.en: I won the UNA 2024 Young Leader of the Year Award.
lines.zh: 我獲得 2024 年聯合國協會青年領袖獎。

slides.ask_en: Today's question: can anyone be anything? Let's find out.
slides.ask_zh: 今天的問題：每個人都可以成為任何樣子嗎？我們一起找答案。

slides.ask_en: In both places, people used to say: “That is not for girls.” Is it still true today?
slides.ask_zh: 這兩個地方，以前的人都說過：「那不是女生做的事。」現在還是這樣嗎？

prompts.en: Stand up if someone has told you “boys don't cry” or “girls can't do that.”
prompts.zh: 有人跟你說過「男生不能哭」或「女生做不到」的，站起來。

prompts.en: Stand up if you do housework at home every week.
prompts.zh: 每個星期都會在家做家事的，站起來。

prompts.en: Stand up if you already have a dream job in mind.
prompts.zh: 心裡已經有夢想工作的，站起來。

slides.punch_en: Look around. Dreams and chores do not have a gender.
slides.punch_zh: 看看四周。夢想和家事，都沒有性別。

slides.body_en: In 2015, every country agreed on 17 Global Goals for 2030. Goal 5 is Gender Equality: girls and boys deserve the same rights, the same chances and the same respect.
slides.body_zh: 2015 年，全世界所有國家訂下 17 項全球目標，要在 2030 年前達成。第 5 項是「性別平等」：女生和男生都應該有一樣的權利、一樣的機會、一樣的尊重。

slides.body_en: A stereotype puts a whole group of people in one box: “Girls are bad at math.” “Boys don't cry.” But a box is too small for a real person.
slides.body_zh: 刻板印象，就是把一整群人裝進同一個框框：「女生數學不好。」「男生不能哭。」但是一個框框，裝不下一個真實的人。

items.en: Girls are bad at math
items.zh: 女生數學不好

items.en: Taiwan has had a woman president
items.zh: 台灣有過女總統

items.en: Boys don't cry
items.zh: 男生不能哭

items.en: Women can be pilots
items.zh: 女生可以當機師

items.en: Pink is only for girls
items.zh: 粉紅色只屬於女生

items.en: Men can be nurses
items.zh: 男生可以當護理師

items.en: Cooking is a woman's job
items.zh: 煮飯是女人的事

items.en: Girls can do judo
items.zh: 女生可以練柔道

slides.note_en: Thumbs up for FACT, thumbs down for STEREOTYPE!
slides.note_zh: 事實比讚，刻板印象比倒讚！

slides.q_en: A boy is hurt, and his father takes him to the hospital. The doctor says: “He is my son!” But the doctor is not his father. Who is the doctor?
slides.q_zh: 一個男孩受傷了，爸爸送他到醫院。醫生說：「他是我兒子！」可是醫生不是他爸爸。醫生是誰？
slides.explain_en: His mother! If that surprised you, a stereotype was hiding in your head.
slides.explain_zh: 是他的媽媽！如果你嚇一跳，表示有個刻板印象躲在你的腦袋裡。

slides.head_en: girls around the world are not in school
slides.head_zh: 全世界大約有 1 億 2,000 萬個女孩沒有上學
slides.body_en: Some must work. Some marry very young. Some are told that school is not for girls.
slides.body_zh: 有的必須工作，有的很小就結婚，有的被告知「女生不用念書」。
slides.ask_en: What would you lose if you could not come to school?
slides.ask_zh: 如果你不能來上學，你會失去什麼？

slides.q_en: At 15, she was shot for saying girls should go to school. At 17, she won the Nobel Peace Prize. Who is she?
slides.q_zh: 15 歲時，她因為主張女孩應該上學而遭到槍擊；17 歲時，她得到諾貝爾和平獎。她是誰？
slides.explain_en: Malala, from Pakistan. “One child, one teacher, one book and one pen can change the world.”
slides.explain_zh: 來自巴基斯坦的馬拉拉。「一個孩子、一位老師、一本書、一支筆，就能改變世界。」

slides.body_en: Taiwan elected its first woman president in 2016. Today women hold about 42% of the seats in our legislature — one of the highest shares in Asia.
slides.body_zh: 台灣在 2016 年選出第一位女總統。現在立法院大約有 42% 的席次是女性——是亞洲最高的國家之一。

slides.q_en: In Taiwan, when a man earns NT$100 an hour, about how much does a woman earn?
slides.q_zh: 在台灣，男性每小時賺 100 元的時候，女性大約賺多少？
slides.explain_en: About NT$84. The gap is smaller than in Japan or Korea — but it is not zero yet.
slides.explain_zh: 大約 84 元。差距比日本、韓國小——但還沒有變成零。

slides.head_en: Strong Women Are Not New in Lugang
slides.head_zh: 在鹿港，強大的女性一點都不新鮮
slides.body_en: For hundreds of years, Lugang has honored Mazu — a young woman remembered for saving sailors at sea. And Li Ang, one of Taiwan's best-known writers, grew up right here.
slides.body_zh: 幾百年來，鹿港人敬奉媽祖——一位因為拯救海上船員而被記得的年輕女子。台灣最知名的作家之一李昂，也是在鹿港長大的。

slides.head_zh: 真的還假的？手比 ⭕ 或 ❌

items.en: Gender equality is only about girls.
items.zh: 性別平等只跟女生有關。
items.note_en: Boys get put in boxes too — like “boys don't cry.”
items.note_zh: 男生也會被裝進框框——像是「男生不能哭」。

items.en: A U.S. law from 1972 says schools must give girls an equal chance in sports.
items.zh: 美國 1972 年有一條法律，規定學校要給女生平等的運動機會。
items.note_en: It is called Title IX. Before it, few girls played school sports.
items.note_zh: 叫做 Title IX。在那之前，很少女生能參加校隊。

items.en: Housework is a skill everyone needs.
items.zh: 家事是每個人都需要的能力。
items.note_en: Yet worldwide, women do about 2.5 times more unpaid housework than men.
items.note_zh: 但全世界的女性，做的無酬家事大約是男性的 2.5 倍。

items.en: Teasing a boy for being “like a girl” is just a joke.
items.zh: 笑一個男生「像女生」，只是開玩笑。
items.note_en: It tells everyone that being a girl is something bad.
items.note_zh: 這等於告訴大家：當女生是一件不好的事。

slides.body_en: Lu Ming trains judo, track and table tennis athletes. At the Paris 2024 Olympics, Lin Yu-ting won a boxing gold medal for Taiwan. Strong has no gender.
slides.body_zh: 鹿鳴培養柔道、田徑和桌球選手。2024 年巴黎奧運，林郁婷為台灣拿下拳擊金牌。強壯，沒有性別。

items.en: Anyone can do that.
items.zh: 誰都可以做。

items.en: That's a stereotype.
items.zh: 那是刻板印象。

items.en: Boys can cry. Girls can lead.
items.zh: 男生可以哭，女生可以領導。

items.en: Don't put me in a box.
items.zh: 不要把我裝進框框。

items.en: Equal chances for everyone.
items.zh: 每個人都有平等的機會。

slides.rule_en: In 30 seconds, shout out as many JOBS in English as you can. I will count!
slides.rule_zh: 30 秒內，用英文喊出越多「工作」越好，我來數！
slides.target_en: Then tell me: which of these is only for men? (None!)
slides.target_zh: 然後告訴我：哪一個只有男生能做？（一個都沒有！）

slides.prompt_en: What is one thing people say is “only for boys” or “only for girls”? Do you agree?
slides.prompt_zh: 有什麼事，大家說「只有男生」或「只有女生」才能做？你同意嗎？
slides.sentence_en: People say ______ is only for ______, but I think ______.
slides.time_en: 60 seconds — then 3 pairs share with the class.
slides.time_zh: 60 秒，然後請 3 組跟全班分享。

slides.sub_en: Vote with your hands — 1, 2, 3, or 4 fingers.

items.en: Share the housework at home
items.zh: 在家分擔家事

items.en: Don't laugh at “like a girl” jokes
items.zh: 不跟著笑「像女生」的玩笑

items.en: Choose clubs and subjects by interest, not gender
items.zh: 依興趣選社團和科目，不看性別

items.en: Cheer for girls' and boys' teams the same
items.zh: 女生隊和男生隊，一樣大聲加油

slides.reveal_en: All four work. #2 is the hardest and the most powerful — it changes what the whole room thinks is okay.
slides.reveal_zh: 四個都有效。第 2 個最難也最有力量——它會改變整個班認為「可以接受」的界線。

slides.note_en: Watch — then tell me one word you remember.
slides.note_zh: 看完之後，告訴我你記得的一個英文單字。

slides.head_en: 3 Things You Can Do This Week
slides.head_zh: 這週你可以做的 3 件事

items.en: Do one chore at home that you never do.
items.zh: 在家做一件你從來不做的家事。

items.en: When you hear “that's not for girls” — or boys — say: “Anyone can do that.”
items.zh: 聽到「那不是女生（或男生）做的」，就說：「誰都可以做。」

items.en: Choose by what you love, not by a box.
items.zh: 照你喜歡的選，不要照框框選。

slides.q_en: In 1893, which country became the first to let women vote?
slides.q_zh: 1893 年，哪一個國家最先讓女性投票？
slides.explain_en: New Zealand! Women in the U.S. waited until 1920, and in France until 1944.
slides.explain_zh: 紐西蘭！美國女性等到 1920 年，法國等到 1944 年。

slides.q_en: At the Paris 2024 Olympics, what share of the athlete places were for women?
slides.q_zh: 2024 年巴黎奧運，選手名額有多少比例是給女性的？
slides.explain_en: Half — for the first time in history. In 1900, only 22 women competed.
slides.explain_zh: 一半——史上第一次。1900 年，只有 22 位女性參賽。

slides.body_zh: 到我們網站的 School Tour 頁面，找到鹿鳴國中那一欄，免註冊、免登入，直接留言跟 Teacher Dom 互動。

slides.big_zh: 每個人，都可以成為任何樣子。
slides.sign_en: Thank you, Lu Ming Junior High!
